notes: W2-5 wait4: rusage is the kernel-side struct ho_rusage (144 B, Linux layout matching src/user/toolchain/sysroot-headers/sys/resource.h: 2x timeval + 14x long). LLVM's sys::Wait (Program.inc:413-468) reads only ru_utime + ru_stime (ProcessStatistics) and ru_maxrss (PeakMemory) when ProcStat is set; the kernel fills DOCUMENTED zeros there (no per-process CPU/IO accounting yet - that is W2-17) and sets ru_maxrss = v1 resident block size in KiB (USER_REGION_SIZE/1024 = 32768; v2: 0, framed pages not counted). Blocking wait4 parks the validated rusage pointer in a one-shot PCB field (struct process.wait4_rusage, appended at end - additive) so the unified reap_deliver_locked fills it cross-context on exit or kill. Bonus fix folded in: x64 waitpid's arg marshalling was reading the wrong regs (regs[0..2] hold rax/rbx/rcx on x64; args ride rdi/rsi/rdx = regs[5]/[4]/[3]); both x64 waitpid and wait4 now remap onto the canonical positions, and the shared core stores want-pid/status explicitly in context[0]/[1] so delivery is arch-independent. W2-10 argv: the two process.h constants are the single source; both trap.c marshal buffers (char argvblob[4096] on the 64 KiB kernel stack), struct process.eargv and struct ho_spawn_ex.argvblob (spawn_ex_pool[64]) inherit the new size (~480 KB BSS total, fine); _SC_ARG_MAX in src/libc/src/stat.c syncs to 4096 (the ONLY src/libc change, per program rules). W2-14 rmdir: fat16_rmdir returns 0 / -ENOENT / -ENOTDIR / -ENOTEMPTY / -EBUSY (root and on-disk '.'/'..') / -EIO; empty-check treats orphan 0x0F LFN records and volume labels as non-empty (conservative, never destroys data); vfs_rmdir maps a routed read-only NFS mount to -EROFS. DECISION: unlink (fat16_unlink) STAYS dir-refusing (POSIX unlink(2) must not remove directories; rmdir is the primitive) - documented in fat16.c. Documented limitation: the kernel does not track which dir is a process's cwd, so cwd-in-use is not reported as EBUSY (POSIX allows it; LLVM never does this). Userland decls (rmdir/wait4 sysroot + libc wrappers) are another lane's job and were NOT added. Failing-test-first: tests written with/for the new code; the LFN boundary test fix was failing-test-first by construction (integrator-diagnosed x64 KVM offset==0 layout). Integrator-decreed standalone commit for the LFN fix (a6dc6c9) kept separate from the feature commit (f0eb59f).
